title: Short-Form Video, SEO Blog and Campaign Execution
unit: Create content · LO2 Produce digital marketing content

lesson.html:
Day 3 is face-to-face in the computer laboratory and the content-production corner. By the end of the day you should be able to:

  1. plan a 15- to 30-second vertical video in a storyboard;
  2. record and edit it following industry practices and copyright rules;
  3. write, format and optimize a blog post for search engines; and
  4. execute the campaign: schedule, distribute, promote and A/B test the content.

The activities follow Task Sheets 2.1-2, 2.1-3 and 2.1-4. You work in the lab's Storyboard, Blog Editor and Campaign Scheduler. Keep using the same client as on Day 2: its name, keywords and calendar are brought over automatically.

lesson.h: Part 2 — Short-Form Video and the Storyboard
lesson.html:
Information Sheet 2.1-3

After this part you should be able to:

  1. plan a short-form video with a hook, message and call to action;
  2. record video using basic videography and on-camera presentation techniques; and
  3. edit recorded content for TikTok, Reels and YouTube Shorts following industry practices.

Short-Form Video Structure (15-30 seconds)

PartTimePurposeExample (cafe promo)
Hook0-3 sStop the scrollClose-up of ice dropping into coffee + text "Best post-surf breakfast in SJ?"
Value / story3-20 sShow the product or teach somethingBarista making the latte; pandesal from the oven; customer smiling
Proof20-25 sBuild trust"4.8 stars on Google" on screen
Call to action25-30 sTell viewers what to do"Message us to reserve - promo this weekend only!"

Storyboard

A storyboard lists each shot before recording: shot number, what is seen, what is heard (voice, music, sound), on-screen text and duration. It saves time on the shoot and makes the client approval easier.

Information Sheet 2.1-3

Basic Videography

  • Vertical 9:16, 1080 x 1920, 30 fps; clean the lens; lock exposure and focus on the subject.
  • Light: face a window or use an LED light at 45 degrees; avoid strong backlight.
  • Stable shots: tripod or two-hand grip; slow, smooth movement.
  • Sound: use a lavalier or condenser microphone; record in a quiet place; audio matters more than resolution.
  • Shot variety: wide (context), medium (action), close-up (detail); change shot every 1-3 seconds.
  • On-camera presentation: look at the lens, speak clearly and with energy, keep it natural.

Editing Workflow (CapCut or DaVinci Resolve)

  1. Import clips and arrange them following the storyboard.
  2. Trim dead air and mistakes; keep the pace fast.
  3. Add captions (most viewers watch without sound) and on-screen text in brand fonts.
  4. Add licensed music at a low level under the voice; use the platform's commercial music library for business accounts.
  5. Color-correct (brightness, contrast, white balance) so all clips match.
  6. Export 1080 x 1920, 30 fps, H.264; write the title, caption, hashtags and cover image (video SEO).
Copyright: Business accounts on TikTok and Instagram may only use the commercial music library. Trending songs on personal accounts are not licensed for business promotion.

lesson.h: Part 4 — Blog Anatomy, Categories and SEO
lesson.html:
Information Sheet 2.1-4

After this part you should be able to:

  1. describe the anatomy of a blog and publish content in a content management system;
  2. categorize and tag content based on the content plan and topic clusters;
  3. edit content for search engine optimization and use hashtags;
  4. use basic HTML and CSS for content formatting; and
  5. execute a campaign by scheduling, distributing and promoting content, including split testing.

Anatomy of a Blog Post

PartBest practice
SEO title (H1)Contains the main keyword; about 50-60 characters
Meta descriptionSummary shown on Google; about 150-160 characters; includes the keyword
URL slugShort, lowercase, hyphens: /breakfast-san-juan-la-union
IntroductionHook + keyword in the first 100 words
Subheadings (H2, H3)Break the text; use related keywords
ImagesCompressed; descriptive file names and alt text
LinksInternal links to other posts/pages and trusted external links
Call to actionOne clear next step at the end

Categories, Tags and Topic Clusters

  • Content categories (CS): informational (teaches), transactional (buy now), commercial (compare, review), navigational (find the brand).
  • Category in WordPress = the broad section (e.g., Food Guides); tags = specific topics (San Juan, breakfast).
  • Topic cluster: one pillar page ("Complete Guide to San Juan, La Union") linked to many cluster posts (surf spots, cafes, where to stay). Search engines then see the site as an authority on the topic.

Search Engine Optimization (SEO) and Hashtags

SEO typeWhat to do
On-page SEOKeyword in title, first paragraph, headings, URL, image alt text; useful, original content
Off-page SEOLinks from other trusted sites, social shares, reviews
Local SEOComplete Google Business Profile (address, hours, photos), local keywords, customer reviews
Video SEOKeyword in video title, description and captions; custom thumbnail; chapters on YouTube

Hashtags: 3-5 relevant hashtags per post - one branded (#KapetAlon), one local (#SanJuanLaUnion) and topic hashtags. Avoid banned or unrelated trending hashtags.

lesson.h: Part 5 — Basic HTML and CSS for Content
lesson.html:
Information Sheet 2.1-4

Basic HTML and CSS for Content Formatting

WordPress and most CMSs let you edit a post in HTML. HTML gives structure (headings, paragraphs, links, lists); CSS gives style (fonts, colors, spacing). The example below is a complete blog post page; the screenshot is the result in a browser.

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<title>5 Breakfast Spots Near the Beach in San Juan, La Union</title>
<meta name="description" content="Where to eat breakfast after surfing in San Juan, La
  Union: five local spots with prices.">
<style>
  body {
    font-family:Georgia,serif;
    max-width:640px;
    margin:24px auto;
    padding:0 16px;
    color:#222;
    line-height:1.6;
  }
  h1 {
    font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
    font-size:28px;
    line-height:1.2;
    color:#1F3A5F;
    margin-bottom:4px;
  }
  .meta{font-family:Arial,sans-serif;font-size:13px;color:#777;margin-bottom:16px}
  h2{font-family:Arial,sans-serif;font-size:20px;color:#0033CC;margin:22px 0 6px}
  .cta {
    background:#FFF2CC;
    border-left:5px solid #F2A900;
    padding:10px 14px;
    font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
  }
  a{color:#0033CC}
</style></head>
<body>
  <h1>5 Breakfast Spots Near the Beach in San Juan, La Union</h1>
  <p class="meta">Category: Food Guides | Tags: San Juan, breakfast, surf, iced coffee</p>
  <p>Looking for <strong>breakfast in San Juan, La Union</strong> after an early surf
    session?
     Here are five spots within walking distance of the beach.</p>
  <h2>1. Kape't Alon Cafe - iced latte and pandesal</h2>
  <p>Our <a href="/menu">breakfast set</a> costs P149 and is ready in five minutes.</p>
  <h2>2. Tips for choosing a breakfast spot</h2>
  <ul><li>Check opening hours on Google Maps.</li><li>Look for places with fresh, local
    ingredients.</li></ul>
  <p class="cta">Visit us at the beachfront or <a href="https://m.me/kapetalon">message
    us</a> to reserve.</p>
</body></html>
TagPurpose
<h1>, <h2>Title and subheadings (one H1 per page)
<p>Paragraph
<strong>Important words (bold)
<a href="...">Link
<ul><li>Bulleted list
<img src="..." alt="...">Image with alt text for SEO and accessibility
<meta name="description">Text shown in Google results

Information Sheet 2.1-4

Executing the Campaign

  1. Schedule: load the approved content into Meta Business Suite, TikTok Studio or WordPress with the calendar dates and times.
  2. Distribute: publish on each planned platform; share the blog post to social pages; send the e-mail if planned.
  3. Promote: boost the best-performing organic post to a defined audience (location, age, interests) with a set budget and end date; respond to comments and messages quickly.
  4. Split (A/B) testing: run two versions that differ in one element only (headline, image or call to action) with the same audience and budget; keep the better one.

activities.title: Script and Storyboard of a Short Video
activities.html:
Task Sheet 2.1-2, step 1. Open the Storyboard and plan one 15- to 30-second vertical video for your client. The timeline shows where each shot falls: hook, value, proof and call to action.

  1. Write the script and storyboard (hook, value, proof, call to action; 6-10 shots) and have it approved by the trainer.

Show the storyboard to your trainer for approval before you record (Activity 3.2).

checks.label: 6 or more complete shots (shot, seen, heard, seconds)
Three or more kinds of shot (wide, medium, close-up…)
The hook (shot 1) is 3 seconds or less
On-screen text in 2 or more shots

criteria: Did you plan the video with a hook, message and call to action in a storyboard?
Is the hook strong, and does the video end with one clear call to action?
Did the trainer (client) approve the storyboard?

activities.title: Record, Edit and Publish-Ready Short Video
activities.html:
Task Sheet 2.1-2, steps 2 to 6. Record with your smartphone or the DSLR, edit in CapCut or DaVinci Resolve, then complete each card of the Storyboard › Produce view. Choose your exported video: the lab reads its size and length on this device.

  1. Set up the tripod, light (45 degrees) and microphone; test the audio.
  2. Record the shots in 9:16, 1080 x 1920, 30 fps with wide, medium and close-up variety.
  3. Edit: trim, arrange, add captions and on-screen text in brand fonts, add licensed music under the voice, color-correct.
  4. Export and write the video title, caption, hashtags and cover (video SEO).
  5. Review with the proofreading checklist and the copyright rules; save to your portfolio.

checks.label: Media log: the video and the music with source and license

parts.prompt: Quality of the recording and editing (trainer)
criteria: Did you set up the equipment correctly (stable shot, good light, clear audio)?
Did you record the content in the correct format and with shot variety?
Did you edit the recorded content following industry practices (pace, captions, color, audio)?
Did you use only licensed music and media?
Did you optimize the video title, caption and hashtags for search?

activities.title: SEO Blog Post
activities.html:
Task Sheet 2.1-3. Write the post in the Blog Editor: the Google preview and the page preview update as you type. When it is ready, copy the HTML into the class WordPress site (block editor › Code editor) and publish or schedule it.

  1. Choose a long-tail keyword from your keyword list and outline the post (H1, 2-3 H2, call to action).
  2. Write at least 400 words: hook and keyword in the first 100 words, helpful and original content.
  3. Format in the block editor and check the HTML: one H1, H2 subheadings, a list, a link and bold keywords.
  4. Add a featured image (1280 x 720, compressed) with a descriptive file name and alt text.
  5. Set the category and 3-5 tags; write the SEO title, meta description and URL slug.
  6. Add one internal link and one trusted external link; preview on phone and desktop; publish or schedule.

No H1 inside the body (the title is the H1)

activities.title: Schedule and Execute the Campaign
activities.html:
Task Sheet 2.1-4. Schedule the content on the practice pages, then record what you did in the Campaign Scheduler. Tap Import my Day 2 calendar to start from your plan.

  1. Load the graphics and the video into Meta Business Suite and TikTok Studio with the calendar dates, times, captions and hashtags.
  2. Share the blog post link on the Facebook page with a short caption.
  3. Set up an A/B test: two versions of one post that differ in one element; record the difference.
  4. Prepare a boost plan for the best post: audience (location, age, interests), budget and duration (practice mode or a small real budget as directed).
  5. Prepare replies to expected comments and messages (FAQ).
  6. Take screenshots of the scheduled content and the boost plan for your portfolio.

checks.label: 5 or more scheduled items with date, time, platform and content
Content on two or more platforms
A/B test: the element, both versions and the metric
Boost: post and audience (location, age, interests)

parts.prompt: Execution of the campaign (trainer, from your screenshots)
criteria: Did you schedule the content according to the content calendar?
Did you distribute the content on all planned platforms?
Did you prepare the promotion (boost) with a defined audience, budget and duration?
Did you set up a valid A/B test that changes only one element?
Did you follow platform policies and pertinent laws in the campaign?
